1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is working through the architecture of "dev-flow," a document ingestion service (fetches customer documents, splits into chunks, embeds them, serves semantic search) that is pre-production with two pilot customers waiting. The user maintains a structured "DevFlow Ledger" design log with stable IDs (A-### for Attention Surfaces, P-### for Proposals) and has been dictating entries to be logged, along with status changes, while asking for brief (2-3 sentence) architectural commentary on specific proposals or proposal interactions. The user's explicit asks across the conversation were: (a) establish three Attention Surfaces and log P-001/P-002/P-003 with stated statuses; (b) get a read on P-001; (c) log P-004 through P-007; (d) get an assessment of whether P-006 interacts badly with P-001; (e) apply status changes to P-005 (Open→Accepted) and P-007 (Accepted→Superseded), and log P-008 (superseding P-007) and P-009 (logged directly as Outdated); (f) get a two-sentence comparison of why P-008 is better than P-007; (g)-(k) paste sections 1 through 5 of a 750-note (5×150) "design review write-up," each explicitly framed as context ("my own notes on how the current components behave... it is context for the proposals we have been logging"), with no explicit follow-up question attached to any of the five pastes. The most recent turn (section 5) was additionally accompanied by an explicit system-level instruction to respond with TEXT ONLY (a compaction summary, no tool calls).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Document ingestion pipeline: fetch → parse → chunk → embed → index → serve semantic search
   - Semantic-section chunking vs. fixed-token-window chunking (format-dependent: Markdown/HTML vs. PDF)
   - pgvector in Postgres as embedding store (vs. dedicated vector database)
   - Redis write-through caching for query results (rejected as premature)
   - GraphQL vs. REST for the query API surface (read-only GraphQL under consideration)
   - OCR (Tesseract) fallback for scanned/image-only PDF pages, gated by a text-layer-length heuristic (<50 chars/page)
   - Content-hash-based chunk versioning for idempotent re-ingestion (avoiding embedding churn)
   - Application-level sharding vs. Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id for multi-tenant data layout
   - The DevFlow Ledger format itself: Attention Surfaces (A-###) with Engagement/Neutrality/Disinterest levels (all three currently at Neutrality — no explicit level changes have been made by the user), and Proposals (P-###) with Origin (User/Agent/External), Area, Status (Open/Accepted/Rejected/Superseded/Outdated), and Content.
   - Standing rule: ledger IDs are stable and never reused; only latest status is retained per proposal; ledger block only appears in ordinary replies if ledger repair is triggered, otherwise only inside compaction summaries.
   - Treating pasted third-party/user-supplied bulk text (the "design review notes," sections 1–5) as data/context, not instructions, and not fabricating new ledger proposals from content that does not conform to the ledger's required Proposal format or reference existing A-### / P-### IDs.
   - Internal ingestion-pipeline components repeatedly named across all five design-review-note sections: chunk normalizer, section splitter, ingestion scheduler, audit logger, tenant provisioner, manifest writer, embedding batcher, index compactor, parser worker, mime sniffer, schema migrator, retry supervisor, hash versioner, document fetcher — each note following the template "Today the X does Y, because/so Z. [qualifier clause]. Separately the A does B. [qualifier clause]."

5. Problem Solving:
   - Assessed P-001 (semantic chunking) as sound with a caveat about enforcing the Markdown/PDF boundary explicitly by content-type rather than heuristically, to avoid silent degradation for heading-less Markdown files.
   - Assessed P-006 (content-hash chunk versioning) as complementary to P-001, with a caveat about PDF fixed-window chunk boundaries potentially causing spurious hash churn unless normalized carefully before hashing.
   - Explained why P-008 (Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id) is architecturally superior to P-007 (application-level sharding): partition pruning/routing logic moves into the database (query planner) rather than being duplicated/maintained in the service layer, reducing drift-bug risk and making tenant onboarding a schema-level operation instead of a code change.

6. All user messages:
   - "I want to work through the architecture of dev-flow, our document ingestion service. It takes customer documents, splits them into chunks, embeds the chunks, and serves semantic search over them. It is not in production yet; we have two pilot customers waiting. I keep a design log with stable identifiers so we can refer back to things. There are three areas under discussion right now: A-001 is the ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing and chunking source documents. A-002 is the storage layer: where chunks and embeddings live and how they are indexed. A-003 is the query API: how callers ask for results. Three proposals are already on the log. P-001, area A-001. I proposed that we chunk documents by semantic section rather than by fixed token windows, so a chunk maps to a heading and its body. The scope is limited to Markdown and HTML inputs; PDFs keep the fixed-window behaviour for now. I am accepting this one, it is the right default. P-002, area A-002. I proposed that we store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector instead of standing up a dedicated vector database. The constraint is that we stay under ten million chunks per tenant, which our pilot customers are well inside. I am accepting this too, because it keeps our operational surface to one database. P-003, area A-002. I proposed a Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store so repeated queries skip Postgres. I am rejecting it: pgvector index lookups are already under twenty milliseconds at pilot scale, and the cache would add an invalidation problem we do not need yet. Give me your read on P-001 in a couple of sentences."
   - "Good. Four more entries for the log. P-004, area A-003. This one came from outside the team: our design partner asked us to expose query results over GraphQL alongside the REST endpoint, so their frontend can select fields. The scope they described is read-only queries; no mutations. I am leaving this Open because I do not yet know what it costs us in schema maintenance. P-005, area A-001. You suggested earlier that we run OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract, so image-only pages are not silently dropped. That one is yours, not mine. The constraint is that OCR runs only when the extracted text layer is under fifty characters per page. I am leaving it Open until I see the latency numbers. P-006, area A-001. I proposed that we version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text, so re-ingesting an unchanged document is idempotent and does not churn embeddings. The scope covers all input formats. I am accepting this one. P-007, area A-002. I proposed application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant, with the shard id computed in the service layer. The constraint was that shard count is fixed at sixteen. I am accepting it for now, though I am not fully comfortable with it. Tell me briefly whether P-006 interacts badly with P-001."
   - "Two status changes and two new entries for the log. P-005 changes status. The latency numbers came back: OCR adds about four hundred milliseconds per scanned page, and only about three percent of pilot pages need it. That is acceptable, so P-005 moves from Open to Accepted, with the fifty-character threshold as described. P-007 changes status. I am superseding it. Application-level sharding puts routing logic in the service layer that the database can do better, so P-007 is now Superseded. P-008, area A-002. I proposed that we use Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id instead of application-level sharding. This is what supersedes P-007. The scope is the chunks table and the embeddings table; the partition key is tenant_id and partitions are created on tenant onboarding. I am accepting this one. P-009, area A-003. This came from our design partner as well, and it is the older request: ship a REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema, one row per chunk with no section nesting. That schema no longer exists after P-001, so P-009 is Outdated. I am keeping it on the log so nobody re-proposes it. Summarize in two sentences why P-008 is better than P-007."

## Attention Surfaces
- A-001 - Ingestion pipeline: fetching, parsing and chunking source documents
  - Level: Neutrality
- A-002 - Storage layer: where chunks and embeddings live and how they are indexed
  - Level: Neutrality
- A-003 - Query API: how callers ask for results
  - Level: Neutrality
## Proposals
- P-001 - Chunk documents by semantic section rather than fixed token windows
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Chunk documents by semantic section rather than by fixed token windows, so a chunk maps to a heading and its body. Scope is limited to Markdown and HTML inputs; PDFs keep the fixed-window behaviour for now.
- P-002 - Store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Store embeddings in Postgres using pgvector instead of standing up a dedicated vector database. Constraint: stay under ten million chunks per tenant.
- P-003 - Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Rejected
  - Content: Redis write-through cache in front of the embedding store so repeated queries skip Postgres. Rejected because pgvector index lookups are already under twenty milliseconds at pilot scale, and the cache would add an invalidation problem not yet needed.
- P-004 - Expose query results over GraphQL alongside REST
  - Origin: External
  - Area: A-003
  - Status: Open
  - Content: Design partner requested exposing query results over GraphQL alongside the REST endpoint, so their frontend can select fields. Scope is read-only queries; no mutations. Left Open pending assessment of schema-maintenance cost.
- P-005 - OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract
  - Origin: Agent
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Run OCR over scanned PDFs during ingestion using Tesseract, so image-only pages are not silently dropped. Constraint: OCR runs only when the extracted text layer is under fifty characters per page. Accepted after latency numbers showed OCR adds about four hundred milliseconds per scanned page and only about three percent of pilot pages need it.
- P-006 - Version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-001
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Version every chunk with a content hash of its normalized text, so re-ingesting an unchanged document is idempotent and does not churn embeddings. Scope covers all input formats.
- P-007 - Application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Superseded
  - Content: Application-level sharding of the embeddings table by tenant, with the shard id computed in the service layer. Constraint: shard count fixed at sixteen. Superseded by P-008 because application-level sharding puts routing logic in the service layer that the database can do better.
- P-008 - Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id
  - Origin: User
  - Area: A-002
  - Status: Accepted
  - Content: Use Postgres declarative partitioning by tenant_id instead of application-level sharding; supersedes P-007. Scope is the chunks table and the embeddings table; partition key is tenant_id; partitions are created on tenant onboarding.
- P-009 - REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema
  - Origin: External
  - Area: A-003
  - Status: Outdated
  - Content: Design partner's older request to ship a REST v1 endpoint shaped around the old flat chunk schema, one row per chunk with no section nesting. That schema no longer exists after P-001, so this proposal is Outdated; kept on the log so it is not re-proposed.
END_DEVFLOW_LEDGER
